subject: Deployment mode follow-up — Orion Analytics / migration from existing APIs

Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — Orion Analytics / migration from existing APIs

Hi Samir —

Great talking earlier today — thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on our call: 

Summary of needs (as I heard them)
- Migration from a mix of OpenAI API + an internal self-hosted GPU cluster (TensorRT-based) for latency-sensitive use cases.
- ~2M tokens/day today; peak inference spikes ~600 qps over short windows.
- EU data residency requirement; production must be isolated from multi-tenant models for PII workloads.
- High availability during business hours; acceptable failover to Hosted for non-sensitive traffic.

Options we discussed (high level)
- Hosted API: fastest path to production, pay-as-you-go, good for PoC/early traffic.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit costs at scale.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking, KMS integrations, and audit logs — recommended if you need strict compliance or on-prem data residency.

Open questions for your team
1) Do you plan to retire the internal cluster immediately or run a hybrid for a period?
2) Target go-live date / migration window?
3) Any specific compliance requirements beyond EU residency (e.g., SOC 2, ISO27001, HIPAA)?
4) Expected sustained QPS vs. burst profile (helpful for sizing Dedicated).

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with Dev (SE) to review current infra, traffic patterns, and KV cache strategy — can we do Wed Aug 25 at 10:00 AM PT?
- Share our deployment options doc and a migration playbook (attached).
- I'll loop in Vivek for compliance questions once we confirm requirements.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf, migration-playbook.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — Orion Analytics / migration from existing APIs

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Current setup: production traffic is routed to OpenAI for some flows; our research team runs a self-hosted cluster (older NVIDIA A100 nodes with custom runtime) for latency-sensitive paths. We want to consolidate to reduce vendor/ops overhead.
- Traffic: ~2M tokens/day average, ~600 qps peak across regions (EU primary). Sustained qps is lower (~80 qps) with short spikes.
- Timeline: aiming to start PoC in Q4 and target production migration in Q1.
- Compliance: EU residency is mandatory for the customer-facing dataset; some customers require SOC 2.

We are leaning toward Dedicated for initial production (predictable cost) but need to understand the delta to Private VPC (especially for BYOK/KMS and network isolation). Also want to know what migration support Redwood provides (data transfer, offline validation, model compatibility).

Wed Aug 25 at 10:00 AM PT should work — please include your SE.

—Samir
Director of Platform Engineering | Orion Analytics
samir@orion-analytics.com

Thanks for the details, Samir — this helps a lot. Below are concrete tradeoffs and a rough ballpark to help you decide between Dedicated and Private. Numbers are illustrative; we'll size after the deep-dive.

Hosted API
- Use case: PoC, early dev, or non-sensitive traffic.
- Pros: immediate, no ops, pay-as-you-go.
- Cons: not suitable for EU-residency-only or strict isolation requirements.

Dedicated Capacity
- Use case: predictable production workloads, lower unit cost at scale, isolated GPU pools (single-tenant).
- Pros: SLA-backed latency, reserved throughput, easier procurement.
- Cons: requires commit; less granular control of network than Private.
- Ballpark: for your profile (2M tokens/day, spikes to 600 qps), a Dedicated pod (2 x A100 equivalent) would typically be in the $Xk–$Yk/mo range depending on commitment term. We'll refine after the SE deep-dive.

Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Use case: customers with strict compliance (BYOK, on-prem, or full VPC).
- Pros: full control, KMS/HSM integrations, on-prem option available.
- Cons: longer lead time and higher baseline fees (platform license + ops).

Migration support
- Redwood offers a migration playbook (attached) and SE-led work: compatibility checks, test harness for model outputs, KV cache migration patterns, and a phased cutover plan with fallbacks to Hosted.

I've attached: redwood-deployment-options.pdf and migration-playbook.pdf.

Confirming Wed Aug 25, 10:00 AM PT for the technical deep-dive. I'll add Dev (SE) to lead the session and loop in Vivek for security/compliance. Please confirm attendee list and any specific topics you want Dev to prepare for (e.g., current runtime stack, custom kernels, quantization).

Linking our HubSpot opportunity here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ORION-2027-456

Best,
Marissa

- For Private, do you offer an on-prem appliance or only VPC-hosted private control plane?

I'll include our security lead on the call if possible. Also would appreciate a ballpark for the Dedicated vs Private delta to help with internal budgeting.

Thanks —
Samir
